title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up an abstract framework. Its handwriting appears on the back of a typescript page from SGA 7 Exp. IX (Néron models and the monodromy pairing), but the mathematics is unrelated to that typescript.

(1)-(2) S is a Z-graded ring (commutativity marked, apparently 'commutatif') concentrated in degrees >= 0, S = ⊕_{n>=0} S_n, and k = S_0.

(3) M = Modgrad(S) is the abelian category of graded S-modules with degree-preserving maps.

(4) The translation functor t is defined by t(M)_i = M_{i+1}. It is an automorphism of M, and one writes M[i] = t^i(M).

(5) For each integer N there are two strictly full subcategories:
- M_N = {P : P_i = 0 for i < N};
- M^N = {P : P_i = 0 for i > N}.
The M_N decrease and the M^N increase as N increases.

(6) t^i(M_N) = M_{N-i} and t^i(M^N) = M^{N-i}. Hence (6.1) M_N = t^{-N} M_0 and M^N = t^{-N} M^0.

(7)-(8.1) So the two filtered families of subcategories are equivalent to the single pair (M_0, M^0) together with t.

Final remark: M_N and M^{N-1} determine each other. Therefore M_0 (or M^0) alone recovers all the M_N and M^N.

In modern terms, (M_N, M^{N-1}) is a torsion pair (torsion theory) in the abelian category M:
- Hom(M_N, M^{N-1}) = 0.
- Because S has degrees >= 0, P_{>=N} is a submodule of P. Every P therefore sits in an exact sequence 0 -> P_{>=N} -> P -> P/P_{>=N} -> 0, with first term in M_N and last term in M^{N-1}.
- Each class is the orthogonal of the other. Test with the free modules S(-i) to get one direction, and with the quotients P/P_{>i} for the other.
The whole structure is a translation-compatible family of torsion pairs: a 't-structure on an abelian category with shift'. It is the kind of axiomatics one would need to treat graded modules over (divided-power or Koszul-type) algebras abstractly, presumably in service of the divided-power de Rham complex of the folder title.
errors: (8.1) as transcribed has the inclusions reversed. From (6), t M_0 = M_{-1} ⊃ M_0 and t M^0 = M^{-1} ⊂ M^0. So the correct statement is t M_0 ⊃ M_0 and t M^0 ⊂ M^0. Either the handwriting or the transcription has inverted them; the symbols are hard to read.

The claim that M_N and M^{N-1} determine each other is stated without proof. It is true, and uses essentially that S is concentrated in nonnegative degrees: P_{>=N} must be a submodule. Without that hypothesis the stated mutual determination as orthogonals would still hold via free modules and truncations only partially.

ideas.what: Category of graded modules with the shift automorphism t, M[i] = t^i M
Subcategories of modules concentrated in degrees >= N or <= N, permuted by the shift
ideas.modern_name: torsion pair / truncation, analogous to a t-structure compatible with shift

ideas.what: The pair (M_0, M^0) with t determines all M_N, M^N; M_N and M^{N-1} are mutual orthogonals
ideas.modern_name: torsion pair determined by one class; shift-stable torsion class

missed.claim: The page begins an axiomatization of a graded module category through intrinsic data: an abelian category with an automorphism t and a t-stable family of torsion pairs. It hints at a 'filtered/graded abelian category with shift' formalism. The thread breaks off here; whether it continues elsewhere in cote 136 is unknown from this page.
missed.quote: La catégorie M, munie déjà de l'automorphisme t, se trouve munie des familles (M_N) et (M^N)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mildly reminiscent of later abstract notions (Beilinson's f-categories, t-structures compatible with a shift). But the content itself is elementary and well known, so it is of low interest.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary setup of graded modules, the shift functor, and degree truncations (a torsion pair). Everything is standard; the only interest is the abstract phrasing as structures on a category with an automorphism.
transcription_corrections: 'S = Σ S_n^♮' is better read as S = ⊕_{n>=0} S_n; the superscript mark is likely spurious. Likewise 'k = S_0'.
'avec leurs inclusions d'inclusion [?]' probably reads 'liées par des inclusions' (or similar).
'équivalent ; elles sont du couple' should read roughly 'équivaut [à la donnée] du couple'.
'On ne voit d'ailleurs comment' should read 'On voit d'ailleurs comment M_N, M^{N-1} se déterminent mutuellement, donc M_0 ou M^0 permet de retrouver tous les M_N, M^N'.
In (8.1) the inclusion symbols are ambiguous; mathematically they should be t M_0 ⊃ M_0 and t M^0 ⊂ M^0.
The archive folio number at the bottom is 288.
